steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Thank you very much for helping me out with gathering herbs, Ms. Utage, Ms. Beanstalk.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: There is no way I could've found nearly this many without the two of you...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Oh, it's no biggie. I don't go on field ops much. It's a great change of pace.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: And, geez. Just call me Utage. We're a buncha girls on a trip! Let's make this a fun little get-together!

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I mean, we're friends, aren't we? Don't be so stiff.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Oh, i-is that so?! Friends...? But I...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I... I don't know much about fashion, and I'm not very good at talking... Can I really be friends with you?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: What're you talking about? Of course you can! You're on my contact list, and I can call you any time and go shopping with you. That makes us friends!

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Look, your name is right here, Myrrh.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Whoa! Ms. Utage... I mean, Utage, you know a lot of people!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Huh? What's this list here?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Oh, 'Afternoon Nails Club?' Probably the list I added the most people to.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: What about this?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: That's the 'Group Buy Coupon Club' list.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Um, how about this...?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: The 'Peeps That Don't Do Events But Pay Up' list! Haha, all of them are like my besties!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (If she adds me to this list... I might end up... crying...)

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (She wouldn't do that, right?)
Hey, that sounds like a great group. You gotta introduce me to some of those besties of yours!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Oh, Ms. Beanstalk! You're back!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Kept ya waiting, huh~?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: I got caught up in the road up ahead. It's a little hard to get through.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: By the way, Utage, which list did you add Myrrh and me to? It can't be that besties club, right?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Oh, relax. You wouldn't make it in even if you wanted to.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: You're on the 'Gonna Treat Lunch Some Time' list. She's on 'Medical Department.'

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Huh? Hold on, what's this supposed to mean? I've treated you to lunch more than a handful of times!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Besides, why is Myrrh on such a normal-sounding list?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Ahaha... I don't really mind...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: She takes care of me when I'm sick or hurt. Gotta give respect where it's due.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: (Quietly) Besides, am I gonna get on a doctor's bad side? How stupid do you think I am?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Ugh, can we not talk about this, please? You went up ahead to scout the area, right? How is it? Any more herbs around?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I think we already got plenty, so if there aren't more up ahead, maybe we can call it a day here and go home?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Hmph, I'm getting there! I'll get to the end of this contact list thing...

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Anyway, let me get straight to the point—I did find something.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: I had Trey look all around, and he found a spot a little further north that we haven't been to yet.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Oh, you mean those little pets you got with you? Way to go.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Of course! Hehe, this is nothing more than a walk in the park for my little buddies!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: It's north of here... Going by the humidity, the amount of sunlight, and the terrain, it should be a perfect place for herbs to grow!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: That sounds great! Let's head over there!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Hey, wait up! Let me finish!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Hm... Where's my map for this area...? Let's see... There we go! Take a look here.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: I marked where we are in red, and that patch of grassland is over here.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Huh? This place...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Hm? Let's see.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Oh, are we really that far away from the ship? And what's this say over here...? Ibe... Ugh, it's way too small to read. Iberia?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Iberia, huh...?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: I heard the nomadic cities there change color, and every place they cruise over turns to barren land where absolutely nothing can grow. Not sure if it's true, though.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Huh? No kidding?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: It could be that there are technical problems with their Originium energy source, and that might have polluted all the places they drove through.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: But absolutely nothing can grow there...? That sounds like a bit of an exaggeration.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Oh, that's hardly an exaggeration. There's more. I heard Iberia's cities can even change shape!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: The city plates can all fly away and put themselves back together again! They can even turn into giant, limbless monsters that swallow everything whole!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: T-They can turn into monsters?!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Um, that's not exactly how I heard it...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Why are we talking about this now? Shouldn't we figure out if we want to keep going?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Or what? Is it Iberia gossip time? Hm... Actually, why don't we do just that?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I mean, none of us dare say we know that much about Iberia, right? Let's talk about what we know, then. Maybe we'll figure out something helpful.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Well... I guess we can. We aren't in a rush anyway.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Well, I already told you what I know. Next up, Myrrh!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Huh? I need to say something too?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Of course~

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: O-Okay... I don't really think this is going to be very helpful, though...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Well, I heard that Iberia has a lot of ghost towns...

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: (Quietly) Uhh—This doesn't sound all that different than what I said...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: (Quietly) Oh, hush, just let her talk.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I heard that people sometimes wander into these ghost towns when they get lost... It's cold and scary inside. There are blue rocks spread all over the roads, and there isn't a single person in any of the churches.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: But... if you take a closer look, even though the buildings are all empty, there are jewels built into everything, and the plaza has all these gold statues without even the tiniest blemish!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Jewels! Gold!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Eh, sounds kinda like the City of Gold. My dad used to always sing that song. When I was a kid, I really liked that story!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: I wish that kinda town really existed. A road paved with jewels and gold! I really wanna see that with my own eyes.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Ahaha... I don't think I'd be so thrilled to visit that place...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I heard that in those ghost towns, each and every night, there are things you can't see praying at the church, and sometimes you can even hear someone breathing into your ear!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: On top of that, all the people who stray into those towns feel their bodies slowly turn harder and harder. They start to move slower, just like those old grandmoms and granddads. After that, they even start to talk slowly, and little by little, they lose their minds...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Whoa, that's sounds terrible.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: In the end, they can't move, they can't talk, and they can't think... They freeze up like the golden statues on the streets. Those statues were people!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: ...That's so scary!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Y-You're kidding, right? How is that even possible... That sounds even more out there than what I just said.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: It's gotta be fake. It's a good story, but think about it. How could anyone have spread the rumor in the first place if no one got out alive?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: You're right...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: That's why I told you it wasn't going to be very helpful.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: This is a story I heard when I was still going around exploring with Harmonia... It's hardly reliable information.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Exploring?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Oh, actually... before I came to Rhodes Island, I used to be something of an explorer. I went to all kinds of places with my friends, and the more dangerous the place is, the rarer the herbs there are.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Eh, no kidding? That's amazing, Myrrh! I thought you were totally the kind of girl who, like, shut herself up in her room all day, brewing potions and whatever.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: You're kinda wimpy too.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm not...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: So, it's my turn now, right?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I thought about it a little, and this rumor just came to mind...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Ehh? We are still going with this?!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: You seem really into it...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: It's just a story. What's the harm?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Well, you girls know how Iberia has this festival they call the carnival? Now, the carnival itself isn't the rumor; it actually exists, and I read about it in books before.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I heard it's one of those decked out festivals, and lots of tourists used to visit just for that, but there hasn't been a whole lot of news about the carnival anymore. Some people even say it was canceled.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: But... well... here's what I heard...

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: What have you heard? S-Stop it with that tone. It freaks me out...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Yeah, it's a little scary...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Alright, fine. I'll lay off.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: It's nothing that scary, really. I heard it wasn't actually canceled. It's just you don't get any normal people going to the carnival anymore.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Apparently, on the day of the carnival, bodies start climbing out of their graves, dancing all over the streets even though some of them are missing their arms and legs. During the carnival, all the people in town lock themselves in their houses. No one dares step outside.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: And what if they come outside?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: No idea about that. I heard a few different versions.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Some people say that you'll be eaten alive if you go outside. Others say you get cursed and line up behind everyone else, head into to the woods to the east, and end up hanging yourself.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Whatever it is, it's not a fun way to go out.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Okay, the end.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: So, wanna listen to more of these stories?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Eh, your face's all frozen. Are you... scared?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: O-Of course not! I don't get scared—

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Alright, you don't get scared. So, let's keep going!

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: (Utage looks like she's really enjoying this.)

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Um, aren't we getting a little off topic...?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: That's right!

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Let's not get too off track...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: These rumors all sound pretty farfetched. I don't think they're really that useful.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: It's just...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: It's pretty creepy, right? Is that what you were going to say?

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: I mean, the rumors are probably so unrealistic because the whole area's on lockdown. If you think about it, it's pretty much what you'd expect.

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: So, are we still going north?

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: We have plenty of the herbs we need already, don't we? Why don't we, uh...

steps.name: Beanstalk
steps.text: Why don't we just call it a day?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: Utage
steps.text: Hm? Myrrh, what's the matter? Why are you all spaced out?

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Oh, it's nothing. I'm okay.

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: I'm just a little curious...

steps.name: Myrrh
steps.text: Since there are so many scary rumors... What is Iberia actually like?

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Stop right there, asshole! You're not getting away!

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: José, you shithead! Stop running away already!

steps.name: José
steps.text: Ahhh!

steps.name: José
steps.text: *Sobs*...

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Why are you crying? You fell down on your own! I didn't even touch you!

steps.name: Mischievous Kid
steps.text: Stand up! This is all your fault... You were badmouthing me to the teachers at school, weren't you? You got me in trouble!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I didn't lie!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I saw it, Antonio! You were the one who stole the change Aunt Mirissa left on the table—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You still going on about that?! You little rata!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I... I'm not! I'm not a rata!
Oh, my dear children, don't do that.
Our tantrums, however brief, can lead to mistakes. Don't let your emotions get the better of you. Come, my child, stand up.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Who the hell are you?!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Uhh...!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No way... Um, you..

steps.name: José
steps.text: Um, thank you very much, sir... It's okay, I can stand up by myself.

steps.name: José
steps.text: There's mud all over me. I wouldn't want to get your hands dirty.
That is very considerate of you, my child. You have my thanks.
But you needn't worry. How is mud dirty? Everything we eat and wear is grown from the earth.
Here, take my hand. Stand up. That's right.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Um, sir, you're from the city, aren't you?
Do you know who I am?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: There are rumors all over town that there's going to be an old gentleman visiting us from the city to give a... uh... what is it again...?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: A sermon! That's right! A sermon!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You're here to give a sermon, aren't you?
Yes, very perceptive, my child.
I've been asked to come here to share the gospel with all of you here...

steps.name: José
steps.text: You're a priest from the church?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Yes, my child. I am.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You'll teach us about the laws in the church's book and tell us stories about Laterano?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I will, my dear child, but that is not all I will be teaching you.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The book teaches us that our noble laws are indestructible, and that we must believe it, follow it, and worship it. That is the righteous and correct thing to do... Correct, but perhaps a little off the mark.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I am merely human. In reality, I am no more holy than anyone else. That is why I also have many worthy stories of the people and things around us to share with you. I am here to close the distance between us and the law.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Father, what do you mean...? I'm not sure I understand.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Uh, Father, where are you headed? Is it the village headman's house? I'll take you there!

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Thank you, my child.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: What I say is not important. What is truly important is what you've heard. You don't have to force yourself to understand.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Which way is it? Oh, watch out. Don't step on these flowers here. Give them the chance to grow.

steps.name: José
steps.text: W-Wait...

steps.name: José
steps.text: Father!

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Yes, my child?

steps.name: José
steps.text: I'm just wondering... Did you... see all that just now...?

steps.name: José
steps.text: What did you see?

steps.name: José
steps.text: Did you catch everything... that I said?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: —I'm afraid I can't deny I did.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I heard everything loud and clear from the moment you fell.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Father, sir, I, I—

steps.name: José
steps.text: Father, please! That's not how it is! I made it all up!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I made all of that up! Please!

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You think everything you said is nonsense, but is that really the case?

steps.name: José
steps.text: Antonio isn't a bad person. It's just, he...

steps.name: José
steps.text: That's right! I-I lied! I was just seeing things... That's right! Antonio didn't steal anything, Father! I imagined all that! Please don't take him away!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: José!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: José, stop... stop it!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I-I know it's wrong to lie, but I'm jealous of Antonio. My grades are better than his, but I never get enough to eat. Soon, I won't even have enough money to go to school! I'm jealous of him!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I know those who steal get taken away. I know that. Hugo next door was taken away and never came back because he stole something from the stores in the city...

steps.name: José
steps.text: That's why I ratted him out to the teachers! I was trying to frame him! It's all my fault!

steps.name: José
steps.text: I know what I did was wrong. Please, if you're here to take anyone away, take me! Please don't take him...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: 'We must not deceive others, for the deception deceives even ourselves.'

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: What are you talking about?! No one told you to say that!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: It's me, Father! You heard him! I stole that money...!

steps.name: José
steps.text: Antonio!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Stop it, José. Stop... Stop lying for me.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You aren't like that! When Old Man Pedro broke your leg last time, you didn't lie about that!

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Ah, lies.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Lies can ruin us if we don't follow through with them. This is a most vile thing to do, yet... lies made with goodwill are what make us human.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Go on, my child.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: There isn't any more to say!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I stole Aunt Mirissa's money, but I'll pay her back! I found a job in town that pays really well!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: It's my fault for stealing. I'll go apologize. I ask for your forgiveness and just a little bit of time. I'll return the money when I have it.

steps.name: José
steps.text: But why? Why did you do that?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: ...tuition...

steps.name: José
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Don't you want to keep going to school?! You're much better at studying than any of us! I know you're a little tight on money—

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Tsk, that didn't count! It's none of your business!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Anyway, that's how it is. I took the money because I wanted to. I said I'll pay it back. You caught me red-handed! I'll accept any punishment that comes my way!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Father, you're here to take me away, aren't you? Do it already!

steps.name: José
steps.text: Antonio...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Calm down, my child.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You think what you've done is wrong. In that case, would you like to confess your sins?

steps.name: José
steps.text: Y-Yeah! Let's confess!

steps.name: José
steps.text: If you admit what you've done is wrong, you'll be forgiven, and you won't be punished...

steps.name: José
steps.text: Father, please. Please forgive him. Have mercy on Antonio! He'll be better!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: The law says we mustn't steal or lie. I did both of those.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But I don't regret it. I couldn't think of any other way. I don't regret doing this even if you're going to punish me.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Father, am I allowed to confess if I don't feel regret for my actions?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: That depends on what you think.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: All of us have our weaknesses, and who doesn't make mistakes?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: But when we make mistakes, are we forgiven simply because we repent our sins? Who has the right to forgive another, anyway?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I don't understand...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Isn't what I did wrong? I did something wrong, and I don't feel bad about it. That makes me a bad person...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Does making a mistake once make you a bad person forever?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: If someone commits a crime with malice and then receives the proper punishment, does that really erase that malice and make her a sinner no longer?

steps.name: José
steps.text: Well... no...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Antonio stole money. He has sinned. As for you, José, you lied to me in order to protect him. You have sinned.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Do you think he's a bad person?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Lying goes against our teachings. Do you think you are a bad person?

steps.name: José
steps.text: I'm not... but I've done something wrong! Antonio did something wrong too, but if he doesn't repent his sins, what can we do to receive forgiveness?

steps.name: José
steps.text: Can we condone doing evil?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: No, José, of course not.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Our laws and decrees are the things that set the norms of our society. They are what punishes our wrongdoings and leads us down a path of virtue. In our Code of Law, wrongdoings are never tolerated.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: The law disciplines. It has power, and it will punish those who have truly sinned.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: It may lead us down a path of virtue, but it doesn't always do so with punishment.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: What else, then?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: My dad always says a big stick and a broom does the trick.

steps.name: José
steps.text: The books say... repentance. We need to repent first, then acknowledge our mistakes, and then become a better person...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Exactly, my children.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You know what you've done is wrong. You understand friendship, and you think for others. That is a good thing.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: However... 'Whensoever you point out a mistake, you must first set an example.'

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Antonio, you must first ask yourself this question.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Ask yourself what had gone wrong in the string of events that led us to commit this crime?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Antonio, why did you steal?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Because... I'm not as strong as the adults. No one wants to hire me, so I couldn't put together enough money.

steps.name: José
steps.text: No! Antonio was trying to help me... It's all because I'm so useless...

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I already told you! I'm the one who's wrong! S-Stop crying!

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I understand now, Father. If I were just a little stronger, if I could find work sooner, I would have money, and I wouldn't have to do that.

steps.name: José
steps.text: Me too... I could've worked if I were tougher, and I wouldn't have dragged anyone into my mess.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I am glad to see both of you have already found where the problem lies.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Our bodies are fragile, and so even though our intentions are sincere, we sometimes turn to the wrong solutions to accomplish our goals. Many of our brothers and sisters make that mistake, and it's very regrettable.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: However—We can triumph over these predicaments. This place where we stand is shining so very radiantly because our forebears spread the scriptures of Laterano all across the land.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Its teachings will help us overcome the darkness that the disaster a hundred years ago brought down on us, and it will help us triumph over poverty and weakness.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: My hope is for our followers not to think our teachings a restraint, but to be able to see its most refined form.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This is too hard to understand... Father, what should we do?

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Just keep your faith, and you are doing very well.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: We unite, we strive to be benevolent, and we do good all because these teachings have cleansed our souls. They let us clearly see the benevolence inherent in our hearts.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: This is what I want to tell you—

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: You must believe. You must believe there is strength in your hearts.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Be pious, be friendly, and love others. 'Assist those who need assistance, and treat them well as you would your own hands and feet.' Antonio, you committed a crime to help José. José, you lied to protect your friend.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: It's wrong to steal or lie, but both of you have admitted your mistakes. This small misstep can be corrected in no time.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: I won't chastise you for your mistakes. On the contrary, I must tell you. We must treat each other like brothers. We must let our friendship drive our actions. As individuals, we are perhaps small and insignificant, but our friendship and unity empower us to become something greater.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: As long as we follow the teachings of the Code of Law and uncover its encouragement and calls for us to be benevolent, we'll find ourselves ever closer to each other, just like close siblings.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: This is how we'll awaken our souls and the benevolence and power within...

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: And with this, we'll find ourselves able to overcome every challenge we may face.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Uhh, I'm not sure I understand, Father.

steps.name: José
steps.text: I don't understand either...

steps.name: José
steps.text: Father, this sounds really hard.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: Don't be afraid of hardship or difficulty.

steps.name: Priest
steps.text: It's okay. Even if you do not understand right now, what's inside your heart isn't going to fall apart.

steps.name: Female Villager
steps.text: Reverend Bishop! You are here! The stage is set, and everyone is waiting to hear your sermon!

steps.name: Female Villager
steps.text: W-What's going on? Did these two brats do anything to offend you?

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: No, no. They are very good boys.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: Come, we mustn't keep the others waiting. Antonio, please lead the way.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: R-Right!

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: And José... Come, come with me.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: We'll stand in the plaza and recognize our mistakes before everyone there. We'll make ourselves stronger, kinder, and more glorious.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: No matter what you do in the future, you must first understand how you truly feel. Question your heart as to how you think, whether your impulses truly come from your heart.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: The power that will make Iberia a better place and make us better men is right here, deep in our hearts.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: Remember, children.

steps.name: Iberian Bishop
steps.text: You need only believe in yourselves.
